title: Systematic review of soil moisture monitoring using unmanned aircraft systems
authors:
Lenka Miková (corresponding)
Elena Scholz
Jiří Rous
Jan Komárek
support: IGA grant 2026B0015, Faculty of Environmental Sciences, Czech University of Life Sciences Prague.
rationale: Soil moisture (SM) is a biophysical control on crop water use and irrigation. Satellite and in-situ methods leave a scale gap at field level. Unmanned aircraft systems (UAS/UAV) are increasingly used for high-resolution SM-related observations, alone or fused with satellite and ground data. Existing reviews cover UAVs in agriculture or SM from satellites; they do not evaluate UAV acquisition, processing, and reporting specifically for SM. This review maps methods used in 2019–2026 and audits how completely UAV campaigns report the information needed to reproduce a flight.
objectives:
Primary objective: to systematically identify and synthesise primary research (2019–2026) on SM estimation or monitoring with remote sensing in agricultural settings, with emphasis on UAV-applicable workflows.

Specific questions:
- Which platforms and sensors were used, alone or in combination?
- How were UAV campaigns flown and processed, and what was reported?
- Which inputs, applications, and retrieval methods appear in the priority subset?
- Which reporting items are consistently missing (paper checklist, 25 items + SM module)?
inclusion: Topic, methods and setting as defined by the search groups. Primary research (journal article, conference paper, or book chapter kept at audit). Years and language as set in Search.
